# dsh-usage-stats · Usage Statistics
中文文档 · GitHub · Releases · Issues
[](https://github.com/ailawu0409/dsh-usage-stats/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [](LICENSE)
A community plugin for DeepSeek Harness that adds a **Usage Statistics** section to Settings: token
totals, activity, chat duration, and model share for local sessions.
> **Unofficial plugin:** Not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek. DSH extension APIs may change
between releases. This release targets DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.1.
## Features

- **Overview metrics (3)**: total tokens, peak tokens (single day), and longest chat duration.
- **T
oken activity heatmap**: GitHub-style weekly grid with Daily / Weekly / Cumulative color modes; hove

ring a cell shows the date, tokens, and turns (e.g. `Oct 27, 2026` / `506K tokens · 2 turns`).
- Cel
ls stay at the reference 11px; the number of weeks adapts to the panel width (up to 53, at least 13)

. The summary states the actual range, for example "Active 2 days over the last 8 months".
- **Daily
token trend**: smoothed lines colored by model, with Last 7 days / Last 30 days ranges; hover shows

a vertical cursor, highlighted points, and a per-model breakdown for that day.
- **Model usage**: d
onut chart plus a share list (top 5 models + Other); hovering a segment shows its tokens and share.
- Follows the host light/dark theme and official font, ships a bilingual Chinese/English UI, and pro

vides a Refresh button in the bottom-right corner.
- The page header keeps only the title (host sett
ings title scale, 16px); the settings navigation icon uses the plugin's own bar-chart glyph through

the `settings.section.icon` slot introduced in DSH 0.2.2.
- A failed refresh keeps existing data and
shows one retryable banner at the top.
## Data source and accounting
All data comes from **local session logs** (read-only; no network access and nothing is uploaded):
- Total tokens: sum of `usage` on every `assistant/message` (`totalTokens` when present, otherwise `

inputTokens + outputTokens`).
- Peak tokens: highest single-day usage, using the local time zone cal

endar day.
- Longest chat: the maximum, within one session, of the summed `turn/start → turn/end` du

rations, so idle time across an overnight gap is not counted.
- Turns: counted on the **start day**

of `turn/start`; a turn that crosses midnight counts on the day it started.
- Heatmap summary: count

s only the range the grid actually draws, never history outside the window.
- Deduplication: forked
sessions skip the inherited prefix (`seq < inheritedEventCount`), so they are not counted twice with

their parent.
- History retention: after a session is archived, moved out of storage, or permanentl
y deleted, its folded usage still contributes to totals, peak, heatmap, and model share. The footer
notes "N of the counted sessions are no longer listed". This follows the same usage-ledger idea as Z

Code: statistics do not depend on the session list.
- Failure retention: a failed read or a `migrati
on-required` session never makes accumulated values shrink; the previous result is retained. Only se
ssions that have never been counted are reported as skipped. Failed sessions cool down for 5 minutes

and are not re-read on every scan.
- Session count: the footer's "N sessions counted" includes reta

ined history, so it can exceed the number of sessions currently stored.
- Cap: at most 20,000 sessio
ns are counted; the page notes when the cap is exceeded.
## Performance and cache
- Each session's folded result is cached in `<profile>/plugin-state/usage-stats-cache.json`; entries

for removed sessions are retained (`retiredAt`), so the cache grows slowly after deletions.
- Later
scans are incremental by the persistence `revision`: only changed sessions are re-read (`revision`

is the official change token for derived caches).
- The plugin warms the cache once, 5 seconds after

activation, so opening the page is usually a cache hit.
- Cache migrations run automatically: a v2
cache is upgraded in place to v3 without a full re-read; only older or unknown versions are discarde

d and rebuilt.
- To clear all history (for example, to start from zero), delete the cache file and r
efresh; the plugin rebuilds from the session logs that still exist.

back to the default gear without error.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
There are no third-party runtime dependencies. Tests use temporary directories and fake services; th
ey never touch real session data.
## Known limitations
- Deleting a session does not reduce historical totals (intentional): this avoids the surprising beh
avior where numbers shrink after a delete. Sessions deleted before this version cannot be recovered

because their folded records were cleared with the old cache.
- Token accounting differs from ZCode:
this plugin prefers `usage.totalTokens`, otherwise `inputTokens + outputTokens`; ZCode's `computedT

otalTokens` is `input + cache + output`, so the numbers can differ.
- ZCode keeps raw usage detail f
or 30 days by default; this plugin keeps lifetime totals and limits only the daily detail window to

400 days (used by the heatmap and trend).
- The "Last 7 days" trend actually plots 8 points (today p

lus the previous 7), matching the reference design.
- On a narrow settings panel the heatmap reduces

the number of weeks instead of shrinking cells, so a full year is not visible on narrow panels.
- T
he settings navigation icon is registered through the `settings.section.icon` slot introduced in DSH
0.2.2 (the registration id equals the section id). Hosts older than 0.2.2 do not have that seat and

show the default gear without error.
- DSH 0.2.2 adds German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Portuguese
, and Russian UI; this plugin's copy remains Chinese/English and falls back to English for other lan
ussian UI; this plugin's copy remains Chinese/English and falls back to English for other languages.
